  "title": "AWS Deep Learning AMIs Now Include Optimized Chainer 4 and CNTK 2.5.1 to Accelerate Deep Learning on Amazon EC2 Instances",
  "text": "The AWS Deep Learning AMIs now include advanced optimizations for Chainer 4 and Microsoft Cognitive Toolkit (CNTK) 2.5.1 that are tailored to deliver higher-performance training across Amazon EC2 instances. The AWS Deep Learning AMIs now include advanced optimizations for Chainer 4 and Microsoft Cognitive Toolkit (CNTK) 2.5.1 that are tailored to deliver higher-performance training across Amazon EC2 instances. For GPU-based training, the AMIs come with Chainer 4 fully configured with CuPy, NVIDIA CUDA 9, and cuDNN 7 to take advantage of mixed-precision training on NVIDIA Volta V100 GPUs powering Amazon EC2 P3 instances. Chainer 4 also provides improved support for TensorCores in Volta GPUs used in low-precision computations.   "url": "https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2018/04/alexa-for-business-now-lets-you-monitor-the-connection-status-of/",
  "title": "Alexa for Business now provides shared device connection status",
  "text": "Alexa for Business now enables you to view the connection status of your shared devices in the Alexa for Business console by showing whether they are online or offline. Shared devices can be placed in common areas, like conference rooms and building lobbies, and they are managed centrally using the Alexa for Business console. By monitoring the health status of these devices, you can quickly identify if any of them are disconnected and take corrective action. There are two ways you can access the connection status of your shared Echo devices. First, you can navigate to the Alexa for Business console and choose Shared Devices in the menu. This page shows you all your devices, along with their connection status. Second, you can use Alexa for Business APIs to query the status of your devices. In both the options, the device will indicate one of 4 possible states: Online – The device is connected to the network and all skills and settings have been applied to the device. Offline – The device isn’t connected to the network. The device might be unplugged, or has become disconnected from the network. Sync in progress – The device is connected to the network, and Alexa for Business is applying skills and settings to the device. Sync needed –The device is connected to the network, but not all skills and settings have been applied to the device. This typically occurs when the devices are offline during a sync, and can be corrected by initiating a device sync from the console. In addition to monitoring the status of individual devices, there are two ways you can track the overall status of all your shared devices. First, the dashboard in the Alexa for Business console shows you the total number of devices offline at any given moment, providing you with a quick snapshot of your devices. Second, you can use Amazon CloudWatch to set thresholds and configure alarms to alert you when a critical number of devices go offline. Alexa for Business makes it easy for you to introduce Alexa to your organization, providing you the tools you need to manage Alexa devices, users, and skills at scale. You can view the connection status of shared devices in the Alexa for Business console in all AWS regions where the service is available. Visit the Alexa for Business website to learn more."

  "title": "AWS Service Catalog Introduces the Ability to Chain the Launch of Multiple Products",
  "text": "AWS Service Catalog , used by enterprises, system integrators, and managed service providers to organize, govern, and provision cloud resources on AWS, now allows customers to chain together the launch of multiple products. AWS Service Catalog , used by enterprises, system integrators, and managed service providers to organize, govern, and provision cloud resources on AWS, now allows customers to chain together the launch of multiple products. Customers gain the flexibility to compose products with smaller AWS CloudFormation templates as building blocks rather than creating a monolithic application stack template. Administrators can chain together products during a launch. To do this, the initiating CloudFormation template will call the Service Catalog ProvisionProduct API as a CloudFormation resource, and reference the next product to launch. For example, administrators can create separate Amazon EC2 and Amazon RDS products and then have the completed EC2 product initiate the creation of the RDS product.
